behavior: An inconspicuous ground forager that advances in rapid, long hops, pauses to inspect leaf litter, and sometimes flips leaves with its bill. It also searches low foliage, drops from perches, and occasionally catches insects in flight. Its diet shifts from mainly insects and other invertebrates during breeding to more fruit in late summer and fall. The song is a rich, downward spiral, often delivered around dawn and dusk; migration occurs mostly at night.
field_marks: Uniform warm cinnamon-brown head, back, wings, and tail
Pale whitish underparts with faint, sparse spotting on the throat and upper breast
Plain, softly marked face with a large dark eye and little obvious eye-ring
Straight, slender bill with a dark upper ridge and paler pinkish base
Plump body and rounded head with fairly long wings and pinkish legs
Relatively long, plain rufous-brown tail without contrasting patches
habitat: Dense, damp deciduous or mixed woodland with a well-developed understory, often near streams, wetlands, or other openings. It also uses forest edges and second-growth woodland during migration and dense lowland tropical-forest undergrowth in the nonbreeding season.
